headline: 200 masked men raze Mirpur healthcare center with bulldozers
summary: The Radda MCH-FP Center was vandalized and demolished by a mob, leading to the arrest of four individuals and a probe into police negligence.
details: Over 200 masked individuals armed with local weapons attacked the Radda MCH-FP Center in Mirpur-1 around midnight on Thursday. The attackers took two security guards hostage and looted medicines, vaccines, and cash before demolishing the facility.

The attackers used heavy machinery to raze one permanent building and three semi-permanent structures. The facility provided essential services, including child vaccinations, reproductive health, and family planning for local residents.
DNCC Administrator Shafiqul Islam Khan has called for strict legal action against the attackers, planners, and those who gave the orders, regardless of their political or social status.
Four people have already been arrested and sent to jail in connection with the attack. A case has been filed at the Shah Ali police station.
The DMP Commissioner has ordered a probe into police negligence, as the overnight demolition of the healthcare center took place without immediate intervention.
caption:
200 masked men, bulldozers, and a community clinic razed to the ground. Who ordered the attack?

Over 200 masked individuals armed with local weapons attacked the Radda MCH-FP Center in Mirpur-1 around midnight on Thursday. The attackers took two security guards hostage and looted medicines, vaccines, and cash before demolishing the facility.

The attackers used heavy machinery to raze one permanent building and three semi-permanent structures. The facility provided essential services, including child vaccinations, reproductive health, and family planning for local residents.

DNCC Administrator Shafiqul Islam Khan has called for strict legal action against the attackers, planners, and those who gave the orders, regardless of their political or social status.

Four people have already been arrested and sent to jail in connection with the attack. A case has been filed at the Shah Ali police station.

The DMP Commissioner has ordered a probe into police negligence, as the overnight demolition of the healthcare center took place without immediate intervention.

headline_marked: Police [[detain 289 people from JaSaD office]] in Dhaka
headline: Police detain 289 people from JaSaD office in Dhaka
summary: Police raided the party's central office in Gulistan, alleging an illegal gathering of Awami League members, while JaSaD claims it was a pre-planned organizational meeting.
details: Police detained 289 people during a raid on the central office of the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JaSaD) in Gulistan, Dhaka, on Saturday afternoon.
According to DMP Motijheel zone AC Sakibul Alam Bhuiyan, JaSaD leaders and workers will be released after verification, while legal action will be taken against others.
Police stated the raid was conducted after receiving reports that members of the Awami League and its affiliate organizations had gathered at the office, with 'Joy Bangla' slogans being chanted.
JaSaD has denied these allegations, stating the gathering was a pre-planned central representative meeting attended by approximately 500 leaders and workers, including 30 women.
In a statement, the party claimed they had informed the DMP Commissioner, Motijheel zone DC, and the Polton police station OC about the meeting.
JaSaD further alleged that 500 Jubo Dal members entered the office and created a mob, physically assaulting leaders and workers before police surrounded the office and detained those present.
The party described the claims of an Awami League meeting taking place under the cover of JaSaD's meeting as 'completely baseless'.
JaSaD Office Secretary Sajjad Hossain confirmed that Abu Zafar Surya, former president of the Dhaka Journalists Union (DUJ), was among those detained for being a JaSaD supporter.
caption:
Nearly 300 people detained in a police raid on the JaSaD office in Dhaka. Police allege an illegal AL gathering, while JaSaD claims a mob attack.

Police detained 289 people during a raid on the central office of the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JaSaD) in Gulistan, Dhaka, on Saturday afternoon.

According to DMP Motijheel zone AC Sakibul Alam Bhuiyan, JaSaD leaders and workers will be released after verification, while legal action will be taken against others.

Police stated the raid was conducted after receiving reports that members of the Awami League and its affiliate organizations had gathered at the office, with 'Joy Bangla' slogans being chanted.

JaSaD has denied these allegations, stating the gathering was a pre-planned central representative meeting attended by approximately 500 leaders and workers, including 30 women.

In a statement, the party claimed they had informed the DMP Commissioner, Motijheel zone DC, and the Polton police station OC about the meeting.

JaSaD further alleged that 500 Jubo Dal members entered the office and created a mob, physically assaulting leaders and workers before police surrounded the office and detained those present.

The party described the claims of an Awami League meeting taking place under the cover of JaSaD's meeting as 'completely baseless'.

JaSaD Office Secretary Sajjad Hossain confirmed that Abu Zafar Surya, former president of the Dhaka Journalists Union (DUJ), was among those detained for being a JaSaD supporter.
